hook_text: In Europe five hundred years ago, a small bag of pepper could cost a fortune. Would you sail into the unknown for it?
clip_script: Durban, a spice stall. Pepper, cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg. In Europe in the 1400s, spices came from Asia through many middlemen, so they were very expensive. A sea route around Africa could bring huge profits. Explorers were also curious: what lay beyond the map? Was the sea at the equator really boiling? Portugal's Prince Henry sent ships further and further south. Curiosity, trade and profit: two big reasons to explore.
visual_style: Whiteboard spice stall with heaps of colourful spices, then a long chain of traders from Asia to Europe with the price growing, then a caravel heading south.
mood: Fragrant and adventurous, like a market full of stories.
pacing: Slow at the spice stall, quicker through the trade chain, ending on ships sailing into the unknown.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find three spices in your kitchen and where they come from.
